$comment: Additions to the employment standards edition from the Core HR review (docs/21 §7.2 and §8.1). Merged into rules/employment-standards/ca-2026.json as new keys of each jurisdiction in Step 7, before the edition is tested; a tested edition is never edited (AGENTS rule 15), so after that the keys go into the next edition. Every entry marked verify_at_load stops activation in production until employment counsel checks it, like every other verify_at_load value.

agreement_may_replace.meaning: Which employment standards a collective agreement may replace in this jurisdiction, and how 'never less than the law' is tested. Where a standard is not listed in 'standards', CanDo pays at least the law's minimum even when the agreement's own rule is lower, whatever anyone approves.

fields.standards: standards an agreement may replace when it addresses the matter (codes as in docs/21 §8.1)
fields.always_apply: standards that apply to unionized employees whatever the agreement says
fields.greater_right_test: per_standard | per_hour | not_applicable: the test the statute itself uses

overpayment_recovery.meaning: Whether wages paid by mistake may be recovered from later pay without the employee's written authorization. CanDo's default (setting payroll.overpayment_recovery) is to require the written authorization everywhere; this key only matters when an organization chooses 'jurisdiction_rule_allows'.

fields.authorization_form: what a valid written authorization must contain

exceptions.statutory_holidays: not the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (s. 3(2.1))

agreement_may_replace.condition: The agreement's provisions on the matter replace the Act only when, taken together, they meet or exceed the Act's requirements on that matter; if the agreement is silent on a matter, the Act's provisions are deemed part of the agreement (s. 3(3)).
agreement_may_replace.cite: Employment Standards Act, RSBC 1996, c. 113, s. 3

overpayment_recovery.cite: Employment Standards Act, RSBC 1996, c. 113, ss. 21–22

agreement_may_replace.condition: No one can contract out of or waive an employment standard. A provision of a collective agreement that gives a greater right or benefit than a standard on the same subject matter applies instead of that standard; otherwise the standard applies.
agreement_may_replace.cite: Employment Standards Act, 2000, SO 2000, c. 41, s. 5

overpayment_recovery.authorization_form: Written authorization that refers to a specific amount or gives a formula from which a specific amount can be calculated
overpayment_recovery.cite: Employment Standards Act, 2000, SO 2000, c. 41, s. 13

agreement_schema_addition.$comment: Added to rules/agreements/agreement.schema.json in Step 7 with the families in docs/17 §11.3.
